videos.caption: A heartbreaking moment has emerged from the devastating floods in Nepal after a woman was rescued by the Nepal Army from a flood-hit area. After being brought to safety, she was seen sitting in shock, struggling to process the destruction around her. She had survived the dangerous floodwaters, but the disaster had left her facing the painful reality of losing everything she had. The emotional scene reflects the devastating impact of the floods on ordinary families across Nepal. For many survivors, escaping the water is only the beginning of a long and difficult journey to rebuild their lives. Her silent expression says what words cannot—survival can come with an unimaginable cost. 💔🙏🇳🇵 #NepalFlood #NepalArmy #FloodRescue #Humanity #BetterFromNepal Follow BetterFromNepal for more such stories.

Wildest Festival Yet 🤯🐮 Only in Nepal will you find a festival to do with people passing away, cows, dancing, cross dressing and loads more.  Welcome to Gai Jatra - which literally translates to cow festival.  There’s a huge historical story behind it which is too long to explain here but essentially people originally took cows through the street as a way of saying  final goodbye to their loved ones but now for practicality they use these giant effigies call Tahamacha.  Hospitality of Nepal is off to a fantastic start absolutely loving it here but it feels like there is a festival everyday in Nepal - full video on this will be out on the Youchooobz at some point.  #nepaltiktok #nepal #kathmandu #gaijatra

The road that changed Nepal: how Tribhuvan Rajpath replaced the porters of Bhimphedi 🇳🇵 1950 मा काठमाडौँमा गाडी पुग्ने सडक थिएन। सामान ढोकामा बोकेर भीमफेदी हुँदै पुर्याइन्थ्यो। त्रिभुवन राजपथ कसरी बन्यो — बीरगञ्जबाट काठमाडौँसम्म, सिम्भन्ज्याङको उकालो र हरेक वर्षा पहिरोसम्मको कथा। In 1950 there was no road you could drive into Kathmandu, and goods went on porters' backs. November 14, 2026 Gorkha District, Nepal A large dry landslide occurred in Gorkha District. A mass of earth and rock collapsed from the Gundrung Pakha slope into the Thado Bharyang forest area near Yarubagar. Rocks began falling as early as Friday night, and the main landslide took place around 8:30 a.m., kicking up a massive cloud of dust. Debris reached the Budhi Gandaki River. The landslide blocked both a motorable road and a foot trail. According to the district police, there were no casualties or material damage.
